result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.mutate_edge_attrs_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Transform an edge attribute using a function on selected edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7990-L8080){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.mutate_edge_attrs_ws( edge_attr, func, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies a transformation function to the specified attribute for all selected edges. Supports transforming the `weight` field directly. Requires an active edge selection. Edges without the specified attribute are skipped. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the attribute to transform. Can be `"weight"` to transform edge weights directly. [func]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Transformation function that takes the current attribute value and returns the new value. Called once per selected edge. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `"weight"` is handled directly on the edge's special weight field rather than a generic attribute: ::: {#2c13da4d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.5) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=2.0) ) edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids()) (graph .select_edges_by_id([edge_ids[0]]) .mutate_edge_attrs_ws('weight', lambda x: x * 2) ) graph.get_edge(edge_ids[0]).weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: ::: The second edge was never selected, so its weight is untouched: ::: {#32670244 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge(edge_ids[1]).weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2.0 ``` ::: ::: Selecting every weighted edge first makes it easy to normalize all weights into `[0, 1]` relative to the largest one: ::: {#bf0f7146 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.5) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=3.0) ) max_weight = max(e.weight for e in [graph.get_edge(eid) for eid in graph.get_edge_ids()] if e.weight) ( graph .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None) .mutate_edge_attrs_ws('weight', lambda w: w / max_weight) ) graph.get_edge_attrs("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 0.5, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
